Hi Samir — thanks for sending the sample.

Quick ask: to produce a tight sizing recommendation we'll need a short form you can fill. Below is the minimal intake we use for pre-sales sizing (if you can paste answers into an email or share an edited CSV that's fine):

1) Expected sustained RPS and expected peak RPS (examples: sustained 10 rps, peak 120 rps for 10 minutes)
2) Session model: are requests stateless or do you list per-session KV cache (chat-like sessions)? If chat: avg messages/session and avg tokens/context per session
3) Prompt token distribution: avg prompt tokens, 95th percentile prompt tokens
4) Response token distribution: avg response tokens, 95th percentile response tokens
5) Percent of requests requiring streaming vs short-response (0-100)
6) Target P95 latency for online calls (ms)
7) Acceptable degradation policy: fallback to smaller model / queued delay / error (pick one)
8) Expected concurrency per tenant (if multi-tenant) and acceptable cross-tenant oversubscription
9) Any regulatory constraints: on-prem/VPC/HSM required

A few notes from our sizing perspective (see Marissa's notes below for technical mapping):
- If you have affinity (session pinning) we size for reserved KV cache slots which increases GPU memory needs
- Token mix matters more than peak RPS for GPU selection; attach a CSV with one row per sample request (prompt_tokens,response_tokens,streaming_flag)

If you can fill the items above and re-send the CSV we'll do an internal pass and provide a recommended committed GPU footprint with optional burst lanes, suggested SKU mix, and expected monthly token cost delta.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-29T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic snapshot for dedicated sizing

Adding some mapping guidance for the intake above — feel free to forward this to Samir.

Technical heuristics we will apply once we have the CSV:
- For avg prompt <= 256 tokens and avg response <= 512 tokens we typically recommend an A200 / H100x2 mixing depending on concurrency and whether session KV is used.
- If >50% of requests are multi-turn chat with long context (>1024 tokens) we switch sizing to larger-memory SKUs (A100-80GB or H100-80GB) to avoid KV spill to slower tiers.
- Burst lanes: we size for sustained baseline and add ephemeral burst capacity sized for 5–15x sustained for short windows (configured as autoscale with SLA tradeoffs).
- Batching: we'll measure batching efficiency from the token mix; highly variable token lengths reduce batching benefit and require higher headroom.

Deliverables we'll return after your input:
- committed GPU counts by SKU
- recommended autoscale policy and burst quota
- expected cost range and token economics (per-hour and monthly)
- a one-page runbook for graceful degradation (model fallback order)

Ben — can you flag any current SKU constraints (availability/lead times) for the US-west region in case Novabots wants H100 SKUs?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead Pre-Sales Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
